# `upload_cert`

Upload a PEM-encoded X.509 certificate into a STRUST PSE.

Defined in [`packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/upload-cert.ts`](https://github.com/abapify/adt-cli/blob/main/packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/upload-cert.ts).

## Input schema

| Parameter     | Type     | Required         | Description                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseUrl`     | `string` | no               | SAP system base URL (e.g. https://host:8000)                                                                   |
| `client`      | `string` | no               | SAP client number                                                                                              |
| `username`    | `string` | no               | Username for basic auth                                                                                        |
| `password`    | `string` | no               | Password for basic auth                                                                                        |
| `systemId`    | `string` | no               | Logical system id (resolved via the server multi-system configuration)                                         |
| `context`     | `string` | yes              | PSE context (e.g. SSLC, SSLS)                                                                                  |
| `applic`      | `string` | yes              | PSE application (e.g. DFAULT, ANONYM)                                                                          |
| `pem`         | `string` | yes              | PEM-encoded certificate text (BEGIN/END CERTIFICATE blocks)                                                    |
| `destination` | `string` | destination mode | Required when the server runs in destination mode; an ADT destination key matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]\{1,62\}$`. |

_In destination mode every call additionally requires a `destination` key and rejects the connection fields (`baseUrl`, `client`, `username`, `password`, `systemId`)._

## Output

The tool returns a single text content item whose body is a JSON-serialised object (`content[0].text`). On error, the response has `isError: true` and a human-readable message.

```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "<JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)>" }]
}
```

See the source for the exact shape of `result`.

## Example invocation

```json
{
  "name": "upload_cert",
  "arguments": {
    "baseUrl": "https://sap.example.com:44300",
    "username": "DEVELOPER",
    "password": "***",
    "client": "100",
    "context": "<context>",
    "applic": "<applic>",
    "pem": "<pem>"
  }
}
```

## Underlying contract

- `client.adt.system.security.pses.uploadCertificate`
